a pulsed laser based on the fast reaction of fluorine atoms with hydrogen has been developed and tested.
the pulsed laser based on the F+H2 reaction has been successfully developed.

the following: 1. the study of the reaction kinetics and the determination of the rate constants of the elementary reactions in the F+H2 system; 2. the investigation of the mechanism of the reaction F + H2 = HF + H and of the formation of HF*; and 3. the development of a high-power pulsed laser utilizing the HF* excimer.
the development of pulsed chemical lasers using a fluorine-hydrogen mixture as an initial reagent.
the development of a new type of high-power laser.

this work has shown that it is possible to initiate the F+H2 reaction with a discharge of a few hundred watts, but that it is not possible to initiate the reaction efficiently with a discharge power of ~1 kW.

the results of the investigation indicate that the use of a mixture of fluorine and hydrogen in a pulsed electric discharge is an effective means for obtaining a powerful source of coherent radiation in the ultraviolet and vacuum ultraviolet regions.
the reaction F+ H2=HF* +H is a promising reaction for use in a laser.

the pulsed laser utilizing a fluorine-hydrogen mixture is an efficient source of radiation in the HF* laser range, which can be used in various scientific and industrial applications.
a high-power pulsed HF laser has been developed.
the use of a fluorine and hydrogen mixture as an active medium in a laser is a new method of obtaining a powerful pulsed laser.

it is possible to initiate a chemical reaction in a short electric discharge and to obtain stimulated emission of radiation with a power of several hundred kilowatts.
a mixture of F2 and H2 is an efficient medium for the production of a pulsed HF laser with an energy output of ~1 J per pulse.
the F2+H2 mixture is a promising active medium for a high-energy pulsed laser.
